o: Count adjacent positions where the physical key changes, ignoring case ('a' and 'A' are the same key). Normalize each character to lowercase and count neighbors that differ. Example 1 gives 2 changes; example 2 gives 0.
k: Case-insensitivity means comparing lowercased adjacent characters.
Answer = number of i with lower(s[i]) != lower(s[i−1]).

a.i: Fold the string to lowercase, then count adjacent inequalities.
a.t: O(n) — one pass over the string.
a.sp: O(n) for the lowercased copy (O(1) if folding in place per character).

w: Trivial; the only trap is forgetting case-insensitivity. Follow-up: count presses per key, or handle non-letter characters.
